Name: reward_defect_localization
Title: Reward Function Defect Localization in Autonomous Driving Decision Modules via Counterfactual Scenario Mutation and Driving Invariants
Experiment: Design and implement a novel black-box defect localization framework for autonomous driving decision modules. The method uses counterfactual scenario mutation combined with driving invariants to identify reward/cost function defects without accessing source code or internal reward signals. Key components: (1) Establish 10-15 driving invariants (safety/physical/comfort rules) as test oracles, each following the triple structure (C, Δ, A); (2) Use human or LLM-assisted hypothesis generation for missing features after detecting abnormal behaviors; (3) Design counterfactual scenario mutations that change only one environment feature at a time while locking all other variables (Feature Isolation Assumption); (4) Test behavior against invariants to confirm feature-defect causality using the diagnosis function D(s_orig, s_cf, I). Create 8 types of planted defects: D1 (missing relative velocity), D2 (missing turn signal), D3 (exponential penalty imbalance), D4 (missing curvature), D5 (lateral overlap omission), D6 (multi-objective conflict), D7 (missing acceleration), D8 (goal misspecification). Experiment on Baidu Apollo simulation platform with Scenario Runner. Two SUTs: (a) PPO-based RL planner with defective rewards, (b) Apollo Public Road Planner with defective cost configurations. 5 base scenarios per defect type = 40 test cases total. Compare against 3 baselines: (1) log analysis + threshold-based anomaly detection, (2) classic metamorphic testing (timeline shift, distance scaling), (3) direct LLM diagnosis (GPT-4) without counterfactual mutation. Metrics: localization accuracy (expected 92.5%), average iteration count (1.3), diagnosis time (~15 min/case), false positive rate (2.5%). Ablation: remove LLM module, replace invariants with metamorphic relations. Additional quality requirements: The paper must be written at the level of IEEE TIFS (CCF-A journal). Use formal mathematical notation throughout Section 3 (Method). Include TikZ vector graphics for the framework figure. Use booktabs for all tables, siunitx for units, algorithm+algpseudocode for pseudocode. All equations must be numbered and cross-referenced. Use begin{assumption}, begin{invariant}, begin{definition} environments for formal definitions.

Name: hyperparameter_defect_localization
Title: Counterfactual Invariant-Guided Black-Box Defect Localization for Machine Learning Training Hyperparameters
Experiment: Leverage experiment.py to simulate a black-box ML training pipeline where config parameters represent hyperparameters and quality metrics represent training outcomes. The goal is to localize defective hyperparameters that cause training failure, without access to internal gradient information or loss landscape. Implementation: (1) Redefine config parameters as meaningful hyperparameters: structure_depth → learning_rate (lr), evidence_ratio → batch_size (bs), revision_rounds → regularization_strength (reg), citation_density → model_depth (depth). Add four more parameters for 8 total: dropout_rate, weight_decay, momentum, num_layers. (2) Redefine quality metrics: draft_quality → train_loss, citation_coverage → val_loss, coherence → train_accuracy, readability → val_accuracy, revision_efficiency → convergence_speed (inverse of loss at round 1). Add three more metrics: generalization_gap (val_loss - train_loss), gradient_norm_estimate, overfitting_indicator. (3) Define 12 training invariants (I1-I12) following triple structure (C, Δ, A): e.g., I1: if learning_rate > 0.1, then train_loss must decrease by > 5% per round; I2: if batch_size > 64, then convergence_speed must be < 0.3; I3: generalization_gap must be < 0.15 for valid training; I4: if regularization_strength > 1.0, then train_loss > val_loss (underfitting); I5: if depth > 5, then gradient_norm_estimate must be stable (within [0.1, 10]); I6: val_accuracy must be monotonic non-decreasing after round 2; etc. (4) Plant 8 defect types: D1: missing learning rate (lr=0, no convergence), D2: missing regularization (reg=0, overfitting), D3: exponential penalty imbalance (weight_decay=10, unstable), D4: missing depth (depth=1, underfitting), D5: batch size mismatch (bs=512, slow convergence), D6: multi-objective conflict (lr=0.01 & reg=10, contradictory), D7: missing momentum (momentum=0, slow convergence), D8: goal misspecification (dropout=0.9, underfitting). (5) Implement counterfactual mutation: for each test case, generate 8 mutated configs by varying one hyperparameter at a time (Feature Isolation Assumption), re-run simulate_run, and record metric changes. (6) Implement invariant checker that flags violated invariants for original and each mutated config. (7) Implement diagnosis function D(s_orig, s_cf, I) that uses causal inference: if invariant I is violated in s_orig but resolved in exactly one mutated config s_cf (where hyperparameter h was changed), then h is the defective hyperparameter. (8) Compare against three baselines: (a) threshold-based anomaly detection on metrics (flag any metric outside [0.1, 0.9]), (b) metamorphic testing (double all hyperparameters, check invariant invariance), (c) direct LLM diagnosis (simulated rule-based system that reads metric values and outputs defect hypothesis without counterfactual mutations). (9) 40 test cases (5 per defect type × 8 types), evaluate localization accuracy (expected 92.5%), average iterations (1.3), diagnosis time (~15 min/case), false positive rate (2.5%). (10) Ablation studies: remove LLM hypothesis generation module (use random feature sampling instead), replace invariants with metamorphic relations (e.g., scaling invariance). All modifications are within experiment.py: add 8 hyperparameter config keys, add 8 metric keys, modify simulate_run to generate plausible training dynamics (loss decreasing with noise, accuracy increasing with noise, generalization gap depending on regularization), add invariant checker, counterfactual mutation loop, diagnosis function, and evaluation metrics. The final paper will include formal problem formulation (Section 3 with Assumption, Invariant, Definition environments), Algorithm 1 pseudocode for the localization algorithm, TikZ framework figure showing the pipeline, booktabs tables with siunitx for all numeric data, and numbered equations. This idea is novel (first application of counterfactual invariant-guided localization to ML hyperparameter defects), feasible (fully implementable within the provided code), and impactful (addresses the critical problem of debugging ML training failures in safety-critical applications).
